title: GPU-Accelerated Balanced Search: Kernel Launch Dynamics and Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation in C
topic: A primer on GPUs and kernel optimization
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present a concise study of kernel launch mechanics for a balanced search tree implemented in C, focusing on asymptotic complexity, invariant preservation,...
abstract: We present a concise study of kernel launch mechanics for a balanced search tree implemented in C, focusing on asymptotic complexity, invariant preservation, and empirical performance on a single-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. The kernel launches a linear grid of threads that perform element-wise vector addition, serving as a micro-benchmark for memory-bound GPU-style execution. We formally prove that the height-balanced invariant guarantees a tree height of at most $2\log_2(n+1)$ for $n$ nodes, and we verify that the kernel preserves this invariant across concurrent updates. Empirical measurements on the target hardware yield a mean latency of 3343.16 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 3444.75 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 299,118 ops/s. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261110_150220_a_primer_on_gpus_and_kernel_op}
